dialog.text: Mom, can I get this toy car, please?

dialog.speaker: user2
dialog.text: No, Daniel. I would love to get it for you, but we bought a toy yesterday. If you want to buy another one, you will need your own money.

dialog.speaker: user1
dialog.text: But I really want it now.

dialog.speaker: user1
dialog.text: Mom, can we stop off and get a hamburger?

dialog.speaker: user2
dialog.text: Daniel, it is almost five o'clock. We are going to be having dinner when we get home.

dialog.speaker: user1
dialog.text: Dad, can I sleep over at George's tonight?

dialog.speaker: user4
dialog.text: No, Daniel. We are going hiking tomorrow.

dialog.speaker: user3
dialog.text: Daniel is having a hard time hearing the word no. While nobody wants to hear no, it is something we are going to hear from time to time. The good news is, no is not forever. We hear yes a lot too.

dialog.speaker: user3
dialog.text: When we feel ourselves getting upset, we can take some deep breaths. Deep breathing slows our thinking and helps our brains make better decisions. We can also count down from ten to one to bring us back into the present moment.

dialog.speaker: user1
dialog.text: I really want this toy. What if I take some deep breaths and try to calm down?

dialog.speaker: user1
dialog.text: Thanks, Mom. I just need to do some chores. Then I can earn the money. I will buy the toy car when I get my allowance on Friday.
